description: The quality boundary that a load tier must pass, judged by tools/StackStressGenerator with --quality-boundary. Victor decided these limits; docs/STACK_STRESS_TESTING.md under Quality Boundary gives the reasons. A maximum rule passes when the measured value is at most its limit, a minimum rule when it is at least its limit, and a rule that cannot be evaluated fails.

rules.description: Maximum. The worst simulation tick p99 of every worker interval inside the steady interval stays within the 33.34 ms budget of a 30 Hz tick. The worker's p99 is the upper bound of a histogram bucket, and 33.34 ms is one of its bounds, so the rule passes at p99 <= 33.34 ms.
Maximum. No fixed-tick resynchronization in the worker intervals inside the steady interval.
Maximum. The p99 of the time from sending a movement input to the owner snapshot that acknowledges it, over the whole run.

Minimum. Updates per second of the remote players that walk near a player: each bot counts a remote snapshot record of a remote player whose position moved from its record before, while that record also moved and the player stands within the worker's near radius of 48 m, over the time since that record before, inside the steady interval. The worker sends a standing or far player less often by design, so those records do not count. The rule judges the fifth percentile over bots of each bot's rate, so the players who see the least are judged, not the average.
Maximum. The p95 latency of every gameplay operation kind of the workload; the worst kind is judged. The lifecycle workload has no gameplay operations.

Maximum. Every requested bot joins and leaves cleanly, and in full-stack mode every admitted account logs out. Unexpected disconnects, protocol errors, join and leave timeouts, and admission failures all count here.
Maximum. No unexpected item or corpse rejection, operation timeout, incomplete operation, or failed inventory refresh. Expected revision conflicts stay visible in the report and are not counted.
Maximum. No failed GameService request in full-stack mode.
Maximum. No UDP quota rejection of normal input in the worker intervals of the run.
Maximum. No dropped snapshot packet in the worker intervals of the run; deferred remote updates are scheduled degradation and appear in the remote update rate instead.
Maximum. No missing owner snapshot sequence at any bot.
Maximum. No expired unreleased simulation session in any PostgreSQL sample of a full-stack run.
Maximum. No PostgreSQL deadlock during a full-stack run.
Maximum. Exact item quantities, unique occupied slots, valid custody, and no pending item operation after a full-stack run.

Maximum. How far the average of the last fifth of the steady interval lies above that of the second fifth: the working set of the worker and GameService, which a host pays for, and the managed heap of the generator, whose working set under the server garbage collector follows the collector's commit decisions on a flat heap; the worst process is judged. The first fifth is left out because caches, pools, and the JIT warm up in it. Only a planned steady interval of ten minutes or more is judged; a shorter one is not applicable.

Maximum. How much item_operations and item_operation_changes grew from the retention sample, taken once GameService's Retention:ItemHistory window and two retention passes went by in the steady interval, to the end of the steady interval; the worse table is judged. While retention keeps up, both tables hold about one window of rows and stay level; without it they grow with every operation. Only a run whose window and two passes leave at least two minutes of the planned steady interval is judged, which the soak scenarios' short windows do; any other run is not applicable.

Maximum. The longest that a drift check of the steady interval saw a completed item operation past GameService's Retention:ItemHistory window, and no death event holding it, still in the database. While retention keeps up, it stays within a retention interval and the length of a pass; the soak scenarios run a pass every 15 seconds. Not applicable to the same runs as retained_table_growth.

Maximum. Error and critical lines of the GameService and worker logs, of their standard error, and of the standard error of the network impairment proxy under a network profile, counted once the services stopped, except the message classes of the allow list, each of which names why it is expected in every run, or with duringOutage inside the window of a GameService outage only; an outage entry may name warning lines, which worker_heartbeat_failures and auth_service_timeouts then leave out.

allow.reason: While GameService is stopped for an outage, the worker's registry heartbeat fails every 2 seconds until GameService answers again.

allow.message: GameService does not answer the registry heartbeat
allow.reason: The worker says once that GameService does not answer when an outage begins.

rules.description: Maximum. No failed registry heartbeat of the worker over the run, counted from its warning lines once the services stopped. A failed heartbeat means that GameService did not answer the worker, which then refuses durable actions until it answers again and stops itself after its outage tolerance. Inside the window of a GameService outage the lines that an outage allowance names are left out.

Maximum. No warning, error, or critical line of the worker log that names auth_service_timeout, a call to GameService that did not answer within the worker's timeout, over the run, counted once the services stopped; inside the window of a GameService outage the lines that an outage allowance names are left out.

Maximum. Every account of a login or logout burst ends logged in or logged out within the burst's deadline, after it waited out every auth_busy refusal of the password hashing lane; a refusal is counted and expected, never a failure. Not applicable to a run without a burst.

Maximum. No failed step of the worker's realtime loop and no failure that the loop isolated to one player or peer, from the loopStepFailures and loopIsolatedFailures of the worker intervals of the run.
Maximum. Every bot that was joined across a GameService outage heard exactly one notice that GameService does not answer and one that it answers again. Not applicable to a run without an outage.
Maximum. Every Mob that a bot killed while saving was paused left a corpse that the killer saw within 10 seconds. Not applicable to a run without an outage.

Maximum. How long after GameService answered its readiness check again the worker logged that GameService answers again, from the times of the worker's log; the note also says how long the worker took to notice the outage. Not applicable to a run without an outage.

Maximum. How long after GameService answered its readiness check again the first durable action of a bot, an equip, item move, loot, trade, or gathering start, committed. Not applicable to a run without an outage.

Validity. In every poll round of the steady interval, how late the latest bot's poll ran against the 3 ms poll schedule; the p99 over the rounds stays within half a 30 Hz tick, so every bot sends its input in the tick it is due. A run that fails a validity rule could not measure: the generator, not the stack, fell behind.

Validity. How long a route plan of the steady interval waited for a planner thread; the p99 stays within a second, so the bots walk when they decide to instead of standing. Not applicable to a workload that plans no routes.

Validity. Under a network profile, how much later than its due time the network impairment proxy sent the packets of the whole run; the p99 of the worse direction stays within the 2 ms that the proxy's self-test proves, so the run measures the profile and not the proxy. A proxy that fell so far behind that it dropped packets could not measure either. Not applicable to a run without a network profile.
